column1: # Evidence ledger: one row per claim and the script that tests it.
# Rule: the script must exit non-zero if the claim were FALSE (it discriminates).
# kind:  auto = a script decides | manual = a human judgement, the script always exits 77 | gate = publication, run by verify.sh --publish
# scope: run = reads only the recorded run | pair = needs two runs | host = also checks this machine (tools, cluster), not applicable to recorded evidence
#        tc06 = reads TC-06, which the reference runs (2026-09-29) predate: not applicable to them
# exit:  0 = PASSED  1 = FAILED (the claim is false)  77 = COULD NOT RUN (never counted as passed)
# Results are written by scripts/verify.sh to results/, never into this file.

column2: claim
The running tofu, flux, k3d and kubectl and the provider in tofu/versions.tf equal the pins.
The audit records needed exist, with request and response bodies for the target object.
TC-03 precondition: while a real lock holder exists, a second runner is rejected for the lock.
The run archive matches its own MANIFEST.sha256 (not independent tamper evidence).
TC-01: an update was applied instead of the reviewed no-op, and the API wrote C to A.
TC-02: the same saved artifact was applied to a changed object with an unchanged state identity; the outcome is classified.
TC-03: after the serial advanced on the same lineage, the earlier plan is rejected for the state and the target does not change.
TC-04: after a successful apply and B in the API, the Flux actor changes B to C on the same UID.
TC-05: the four single-writer controls give A,B,B,B with no second-actor mutation.
Two clean repetitions have equal normalized actions, rejection classes and field transitions.
The experiment actors did not write outside the experiment namespaces, and the cluster was removed.
TC-04: opportunity, API call, dry-run and field mutation counts are re-derived from the raw audit records; with zero completed opportunities the check exits 77.
Decision gate: with valid controls, TC-02 or TC-04 supports the hypothesis (0 supported, 1 refuted, 77 inconclusive).

TC-06: a pre-apply gate that looks for drift only in the attributes the reviewed plan changes blocks the saved plan after a second writer changed such an attribute (field stays C, state unchanged) and lets it through when nobody did (A to B).

TC-06: with no second writer, refresh-only -detailed-exitcode exits 2 and the refresh-only JSON reports drift, although no value changed: the provider stores empty maps as null and reads them back as {} on refresh; the obvious gates cannot tell the two paths apart.
Whether the workflow failure is useful as a talk is a human judgement.
The approver identity and the origin of an independent manifest digest need a human check.
The abstract's sentences against the published lab need a human review.
The published repository answers HTTP 200 and has LICENSE and README.md.
